title: Upgrade dompurify to >=3.4.13 to fix XSS advisory GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7
body:
## Summary
npm audit reports a moderate XSS advisory for dompurify (<=3.4.12): GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7. The lockfile resolves dompurify to 3.4.12.

## Expected fix
Bump the root superset-frontend/package.json constraint to ^3.4.13 and refresh package-lock.json.

## Acceptance criteria
- npm audit no longer reports GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7
- lockfile resolves dompurify >=3.4.13

title: Eliminate ruff S704 findings while preserving existing HTML escaping
body:
## Summary
ruff check superset/ reports 4 instances of S704 (unsafe-markup-use). The interpolated values are already escaped, sanitized, generated from constrained values, or integer-typed depending on the site, so this is a hardening issue rather than a demonstrated vulnerability.

## Acceptance criteria
- ruff check superset/ reports no S704 violations, or each remaining site carries a justified suppression
- a regression test proves hostile input still renders escaped

title: Scope the local ESLint plugin to eliminate an npm-audit name collision
body:
## Summary
npm audit reports a CRITICAL malware advisory for eslint-plugin-i18n-strings, but our package of that name is a local workspace package, so the registry package is never loaded. The alert is a name-based false positive worth fixing for audit hygiene.

## Acceptance criteria
- npm audit no longer reports GHSA-55h3-fm53-wq99
- the plugin still loads: npx eslint --config eslint.config.minimal.js --no-inline-config --format json src
